title: Directives and Orders
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapter 12
notes: Operation Orders follow the standard 5-paragraph format; Warning Orders precede them; Fragmentary Orders follow other orders.

rules.title: Orders must be accurate, brief but clear, unambiguous, capable of execution and timely
rules.description: Orders and instructions must be accurate; brief but clear; unambiguous; capable of execution; and received in time to be acted upon correctly.

rules.title: A Warning Order must be clearly defined as such
rules.description: A Warning Order is to be clearly defined as such and should include: the scope of the operation and probable tasks or moves; the earliest time at which recipients will be required to act and the degree of notice; details of necessary preparations; and when and how detailed orders will be issued.

check.where: Subject heading or first line of the order.

rules.title: Warning Orders include scope, notice, preparations and issue details
rules.description: A Warning Order should include the scope of the operation and probable tasks, the earliest time of action and degree of notice, details of preparations, and when/how detailed orders will be issued.

rules.title: Warning Orders should require acknowledgement
rules.description: It is advisable to require a warning order to be acknowledged.

rules.title: Operation Orders use the 5-paragraph format in order
rules.description: Operation Orders follow the format: 1. SITUATION, 2. MISSION, 3. EXECUTION, 4. SERVICE SUPPORT, 5. COMMAND AND SIGNAL.

rules.title: The Concept of Operations states Intent, scheme of manoeuvre and Main Effort
rules.description: Within the Concept of Operations the Commander must state the formation/unit concerned and his Intent, include a succinct summary of his scheme of manoeuvre, and state his Main Effort.

rules.title: Missions are clear, concise statements of task and purpose
rules.description: The mission is a clear, concise statement of the task of the command and its purpose. Where a number of tasks are required they must be linked by a singular, unifying purpose.

rules.title: Missions and tasks use the imperative 'is to' or 'are to'
rules.description: 'Is to' or 'are to' (imperative) convey a direct order; the infinitive 'to' expresses an aim, mission or intention; 'should' may be used only where the commander on the spot is allowed initiative or discretion.
rules.notes: Heuristic: mission statements should express the task in the imperative. 'Should' should only appear where subordinate initiative is intended.

rules.title: All operation and administrative/logistics orders are copy numbered
rules.description: All operation and administrative/logistics orders, whatever their security classification, are given a copy number in the same way as TS/SECRET documents.

check.where: Top right of the first page.

rules.title: Orders state the time zone used throughout
rules.description: In estimates and orders where the format includes the phrase 'Time Zone Used Throughout the Order (Estimates): ...', times in the text do not require a zone suffix.
